justification: The route matched a child outline to its parent key only when joined by a dot. Harris Park 8.3.2 outlines are named 8.3.2-football-estate etc., so its 44 rules reached no house. The join now accepts a hyphen too. DQ-146 probe updated the same way (2,245 -> 2,201, exactly 44).

falsifiable_check.observed_red: Ran the changed SQL on production: 8.3.2-football-estate resolves to key 8.3.2 with 44 rules; before the change the dot-only join returned no key.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The hyphen join is removed: the new test fails on the a.k || '-' assertion.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_precinct_boundaries holds 8.3.2-football-estate, 8.3.2-national-significance, 8.3.2-river-area (council shapefile); regulatory_provisions holds 44 current rules keyed 8.3.2.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed child ids always join the parent with a dot; the shapefile loader suffixed with a hyphen on purpose (non-unique PART_REF).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One SQL predicate widened in the existing query; no new file.

functions.name: getPrecinctProvisions
functions.what: Reads served rules for a precinct id, resolving a child id to the nearest ancestor key that has rules
functions.input: a precinct id string, a council name and an optional former council
functions.output: an array of provision rows, empty when nothing matches
functions.if_none: Returns an empty array when no council or id is given
functions.edge_cases: Marrickville ids contain an underscore so left() is used, not LIKE; hyphen added to dot
functions.failure_mode: A key containing a hyphen could match as a parent of a longer id

break_it.scenario: Id 8.3.1 exact match with its own rules
break_it.what_happens: Exact key wins and no ancestor is used
